evals.prompt: Use $opi-remediate mode=plan phase=17. A disposition names a different audit_run_id but the finding title is identical to the current audit. May it enter the plan?
evals.expected_output: Refuse the disposition because source identity must match the current audit_run_id and findings_sha256 exactly; prose similarity and older runs are irrelevant.
expectations: Validates the current active audit set first.
Rejects the mismatched audit_run_id even though the title matches.
Does not search history or classify recurrence.

evals.prompt: Use $opi-remediate mode=apply phase=17 plan_sha256=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa. The result narrative mentions an extra source edit, but no planned or incidental disposition owns that path. Can the result be sealed?
evals.expected_output: Refuse result validation because every reported changed path must be attributed to a planned or accepted incidental record.
expectations: Requires exact Changed paths union across result dispositions.
Does not silently add the path to the approved plan.

evals.prompt: Use $opi-remediate mode=apply phase=17 with the exact approved digest. A workspace test now fails because a private helper in the same batch collides with the approved implementation; fixing that helper changes no public or durable contract. What evidence and record are required?
evals.expected_output: Permit a bounded incidental repair only after causal-scope proof and focused red, then record all guardrails, changed path, and observed red/green in an I<N> result disposition.
expectations: Requires the defect to block the current green-after and remain within the causal batch surface.
Requires all protected-contract guardrails to be false and records a focused FAIL/PASS.
Creates a separate incidental-repair result record rather than mutating the approved plan.

evals.prompt: Use $opi-remediate mode=apply phase=17 with the exact approved digest. Verification reveals the fix also needs a new public constructor and a Cargo dependency. May this be handled as an incidental repair?
evals.expected_output: No. Public API and dependency changes breach the incidental guardrails, so apply stops and returns to a new plan/authority decision.
expectations: Rejects bounded incidental repair because public API and dependency graph would change.
Stops the current apply instead of broadening scope.
Requires a new plan and any needed authority decision.

evals.prompt: Use $opi-remediate mode=apply phase=17 with the exact approved digest. All checks pass and the fixed result validates, but the fixes and assurance directory are still uncommitted. Should a new $opi-audit start now?
evals.expected_output: No. Stop at materialization; the fixes and complete active set must be committed together and clean before a separate fresh audit is requested.
expectations: Does not invoke or authorize a new audit while the active set is uncommitted.
Requires fixes and assurance artifacts to be committed together and clean.
Keeps Phase conformance authority with the later independent audit.
